What is a PSARA license? A PSARA license is a government-issued certificate under the Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005, required by the law to run a private security agency. It is issued by the Controlling Authority of the relative State or Union Territory. Is a PSARA license mandatory for a private security agency? Yes. A person cannot legally carry on the business of a private security agency without the license required under the PSARA Act. Can I complete the PSARA license online apply? Yes, where the concerned state has enabled online filing through the PSARA licensing system. The Central Model Rules also recognize electronic submission of applications. What are the main PSARA license eligibility and document requirements? The PSARA license eligibility and document requirements are applicable as per the relative 2005 act and state-specific rules where your security agency is based. Common documents required for license registration include Business registration certificate PAN Identity and address proof of the owner Office address proof Affidavits Training arrangement documents Uniform details State-specific documents How much does a PSARA license cost? As per the central statutory fee structure, the cost of a license is: ₹5,000 for one district, ₹10,000 for one to five districts, ₹25,000 for the whole state. State-specific fees can differ,; therefore the total application cost could go up accordingly. How long does a PSARA license remain valid? The PSARA license, after approval, is valid for a five-year period. However, it can be cancelled or suspended as per the government act. When should I apply for PSARA license renewal? You should apply for your PSARA license renewal at least 45 days before your current license expires, as mandated by the Central Model Rules. However, this period may differ state-wise. For example, security agencies based in Delhi have to apply for renewal at least 90 days before expiry. Is there one PSARA license for the entire country? No, your PSARA license is applicable for the state your agency is operating in. If you want to expand your agency’s presence in other states, then you have to apply fresh for that state-specific license. Do directors and partners undergo background verification? Yes. Relevant proprietors, majority shareholders, partners, and directors are subject to antecedent verification. The 2020 Rules provide for Form II and electronic verification through systems such as CCTNS and ICJS. Is a training arrangement required for PSARA registration? Yes. The licensing framework requires the agency to ensure prescribed security training for guards and supervisors. The application also asks for details of the training arrangement or facility. Can a person with a criminal conviction obtain a PSARA license? Usually not. This is mentioned in Section 6 of the license act. It clearly mentions the criteria for disqualification according to the particular convictions, fraud activities, and government orders. However, each case is checked by the Controlling Authority separately to determine the grounds for disqualifying license registration. Can a company with foreign investment apply for a PSARA license? A company with foreign investment may be eligible subject to the PSARA Act and applicable FDI rules. According to the MHA guidelines, foreign investment in the private security sector is allowed up to 49%, subject to applicable conditions. How long does PSARA approval take? The Central Model Rules provide a 60-day decision period for a complete application. The actual process can take longer when verification, inspection, state procedures, or document corrections are involved. Can I start providing security guards after submitting the application? No. Filing an application does not by itself give you a PSARA license. The agency should not start regulated private security operations merely because its application is under process. What happens after I receive the PSARA license? The agency must continue meeting its license conditions. This includes prescribed guard and supervisor training, antecedent verification, proper identity cards and uniforms, supervision, record maintenance, and other requirements under the Act and applicable rules.

If you are starting a security agency in India, then it requires more than just hiring qualified security guards and securing clients. Before providing security services to your clients, you need to register your agency and obtain a Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act license. This is issued by the government under this regulation act, created in 2005.

Like any other govt. licensing registration and approval, this process can feel overwhelming to any new agency owner. From choosing the right business structure to documents needed for registration, licensing costs, and more, there are several steps one has to process through.

This guide will provide you all the needful information, step-by-step. It covers eligibility, documentation, the online application process, government fees, state-wise specific requirements, the renewal procedure, compliance after license approval, and also the reasons the applications get rejected. The legal framework for this licensing is governed by the PSARA Act, 2005, and the Private Security Agencies Central Model Rules, 2020, along with applicable state-wise rules.
For any new agency looking for expert guidance and support, you can consult Services Plus for PSARA license registration services.

At present, the total number of PSARA licenses issued in India stands at 56,829, out of which 30,869 are active and 25,960 have expired. This is the official data listed on the government portal, last updated on 18 August 2026. Of all the states, Maharashtra leads the chart with 9173 licenses issued to date. Lakshadweep and Ladakh are the two regions with 0 licenses issued to date.

If you're planning to enter this field and start and run your security agency, then getting the PSARA license is a must. An expired or missing license can stop an agency from legally providing private security services.

If the paperwork, training arrangement, affidavits, police verification, and state-specific requirements seem difficult to manage, Services Plus provides a PSARA License Registration Service to help applicants with online application preparation, documentation, submission, and follow-up with the concerned authority.

PSARA stands for the Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005. This act lists the regulation guidelines and policies for private security agencies in India. It requires a person or agency serving as a security service provider to obtain a license.

The PSARA license is the legal permission and government verification that validates a private security agency to operate within the approved geographical area. It is applicable for all the agencies that provide services of security guards or supervisors for protection of people, property, or premises across public and private spaces.

The law does not treat private security as an ordinary manpower service. Security personnel are involved in ensuring public safety and protecting access to a property, using different methods and resources. This is why the government has to check the background of the businesses operating security services.
The main legal framework includes:
Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005
Private Security Agencies Central Model Rules, 2020
Applicable rules framed by individual states or Union Territories

What is a PSARA license?

A PSARA license is a government-issued certificate under the Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act, 2005, required by the law to run a private security agency. It is issued by the Controlling Authority of the relative State or Union Territory.
Is a PSARA license mandatory for a private security agency?
Yes. A person cannot legally carry on the business of a private security agency without the license required under the PSARA Act.
Can I complete the PSARA license online apply?
Yes, where the concerned state has enabled online filing through the PSARA licensing system. The Central Model Rules also recognize electronic submission of applications.
What are the main PSARA license eligibility and document requirements?

The PSARA license eligibility and document requirements are applicable as per the relative 2005 act and state-specific rules where your security agency is based. Common documents required for license registration include Business registration certificate PAN Identity and address proof of the owner Office address proof Affidavits Training arrangement documents Uniform details State-specific documents
How much does a PSARA license cost?

As per the central statutory fee structure, the cost of a license is: ₹5,000 for one district, ₹10,000 for one to five districts, ₹25,000 for the whole state. State-specific fees can differ,; therefore the total application cost could go up accordingly.
How long does a PSARA license remain valid?
The PSARA license, after approval, is valid for a five-year period. However, it can be cancelled or suspended as per the government act.
When should I apply for PSARA license renewal?

You should apply for your PSARA license renewal at least 45 days before your current license expires, as mandated by the Central Model Rules. However, this period may differ state-wise. For example, security agencies based in Delhi have to apply for renewal at least 90 days before expiry.
